newsitem.title: USA: Hector looking to sell some investments.
newsitem.headline: Hector looking to sell some investments.

text.p: Hector Communications Corp said Monday it is looking to sell certain investments in order to retire some of the company's debt.

"(T)he company is fully leveraged as a result of the Ollig-related debt financing and is pursuing the sale of certain investments to retire a portion of the Hector...debt," the company said in a statement.
Hector owns a 68 percent stake in the Alliance Telecommunications Corp joint venture, which acquired Ollig Utilities Co in April 1996.

"The company had previously planned to eliminate this debt with proceeds from an equity offering but will forego this option for the time being due to the dilution that would result from issuing additional shares at recent stock prices," Hector said.

Hector reported on Monday first quarter net earnings of $0.06 a share, down from $0.19 last year, both on a diluted basis. Net income includes $1.58 million in interest expense for the quarter, versus $271,082 last year. First quarter 1996 also includes a pretax gain of $687,947 on the sale of securities.
The company said severe flooding in Minnesota and North Dakota has had minimal impact on its plant and customer usage levels so far this quarter.
The company said, however, it is assessing possible water damage to underground phone and television cables as a result of the flooding.
"(I)t may be some time before the extent of such damage, if any, can be accurately determined," Hector said.
Shares of Hector traded unchanged at 102.
